title: Microsoft Teams: pinch to zoom on shared screens
summary: Pass with minor corrections: the rollout, default and sharing controls are supported. The briefing should acknowledge Microsoft's conflicting Mac trackpad guidance, state the general Teams licence requirement and link the command to its PowerShell reference.

claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because Microsoft has not published a licence specific to pinch-to-zoom.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. Replace the licensing notes and the first two licensing sentences with: "Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in the organisation needs a Teams licence to use Teams. Microsoft has not published a licence or meter specific to pinch-to-zoom." In Scope replace "Microsoft has not stated which roles or licences are needed" with "Microsoft has not stated any roles specific to pinch-to-zoom". Retain the low cost rating and narrow its rationale to feature-specific licensing.

claims.claim: Screen sharing mode is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Content sharing > Screen sharing mode.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Meeting policies. ... Select the policy that you want to edit. ... Go to the Content sharing section. ... These settings are described in the Screen sharing mode ... sections in this article.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ScreenSharingMode <value> updates a policy's screen-sharing mode.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy ... [[-Identity] <XdsIdentity>] ... [-ScreenSharingMode <String>]. Determines the mode in which a user can share a screen in calls or meetings.
claims.fix: Keep the command. Change controls[0].api.docs and its rendered Learn link to https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy?view=teams-ps and add that reference to sources. The current overview documents the control and parameter, while this reference also documents Identity and the full command.
